title: Best Practices Guide for Energy-Efficient Data Center Design (Revised July 2024)
venue: NREL / U.S. DOE Federal Energy Management Program, NREL/TP-5R00-89843
notes: Open 48-page federal guide; the backbone of the primer: ASHRAE 2021 envelope table, W classes, UPS/transformer/PSU load-efficiency facts, kW/ton and W/cfm benchmarks, tower and HX approaches, pumping and reset practices, PUE/ERE/WUE/CUE definitions. Text extracted from the PDF on the access date.

title: 2024 United States Data Center Energy Usage Report
notes: Congressionally requested estimate of US data-center electricity 2014-2028 (176 TWh in 2023; 325-580 TWh in 2028), average PUE and site WUE trends, server utilization and AI duty assumptions. Use for macro context and for load-model assumptions. The LBNL-hosted PDF carries an embargo watermark but is the official publication.

title: Energy and AI
notes: Global data-centre electricity (415 TWh in 2024, about 945 TWh in 2030 base case, 700-1,700 TWh range in 2035), regional shares, grid-connection and equipment bottlenecks, and the case for data-centre flexibility. Executive summary page read.

title: Uptime Institute Global Data Center Survey 2026
notes: Industry benchmark survey: average PUE 1.52 (n=644), modal rack density above 11 kW (7.8 kW excluding a few dense sites), 24% of operators with 30 kW+ racks, power as the cause of 56% of impactful outages, operator trust in AI by use case. Use for 'industry average' comparisons.

title: Uptime Institute Global Data Center Survey 2025
notes: Previous edition; its 1.54 average PUE is quoted (and was verified) on Google's PUE page, but the report itself was not opened.

title: Power usage effectiveness - Google Data Centers
notes: Google's fleet and per-campus quarterly and trailing-twelve-month PUE from 2008 to 2026 (fleet 1.09 TTM in 2025; The Dalles, Oregon 1.06-1.10; Mesa, Arizona 1.22) plus its unusually inclusive measurement boundary. Doubles as a tiny real seasonal time series for Module 21.

title: Google 2026 Environmental Report
notes: Covers 2025: fleet PUE 1.09, 83% less overhead than the Uptime 2025 average, 87% of freshwater from low/medium-risk sources, about 35 GW of clean-energy contracts since 2010, demand response and flexibility. Figures and title confirmed on Google's data-center pages; the report PDF itself was not opened.

title: 2026 Environmental Sustainability Report
notes: Covers FY2025: global average datacenter PUE 1.17, 'power harvesting' of stranded capacity, closed-loop direct-to-chip design avoiding more than 125 million litres of water per year per datacenter, WUE intensity down 25% vs 2022, waste-heat reuse. PDF text checked.

title: Inside Microsoft's two-decade push to cut water intensity while scaling for growth
notes: WUE 2.3 to 0.27 L/kWh (2025); direct air cooling with evaporative assist only above 29.4 C; share of hours needing water by climate; plain-language taxonomy of cooling options (towers, hybrid fluid coolers, direct air, air-cooled chillers, closed-loop liquid); Quincy, Washington uses 74% recycled or non-potable water.

title: Amazon's 2025 Sustainability Report: key takeaways
notes: Report covering 2025: AWS global PUE 1.14 (9% better than a public-cloud average, 30% better than on-premises), water efficiency 7x the industry average and improved 33% in 2025, 75% of the way to water-positive by 2030.

title: AWS Cloud - Amazon Sustainability
notes: Defines AWS WUE as litres withdrawn per kWh of IT load (0.12 in 2025) and derives an industry withdrawal WUE of 0.84 from a consumption WUE of 0.56 and 3 cycles of concentration (DOE BMP #10); mentions sensor-based anomaly detection for water and ISO-based PUE methodology.

title: 2025 Environmental Data Index
notes: Tables of Meta's data-center PUE (1.10, 1.09, 1.08, 1.08, 1.08 for 2020-2024), annual WUE (0.30 to 0.19 L/kWh) and site water withdrawal. Latest Meta edition found on the access date.

title: 2025 Sustainability Report
notes: Describes digital-twin models of data-center cooling systems used to forecast water use, a real-time server-fleet utilization metric, and site heat-safety tooling. Good example of digital twins in operations.

title: Closed-Loop Cooling Explained: The Plumbing Behind Meta's AI
notes: Plain-language explainer: closed-loop water-glycol direct-to-chip cooling with dry coolers, air-assisted liquid cooling for retrofits, coolant lifetime up to a decade, and RL cooling optimization now scaled across Meta's air-cooled fleet.

title: Simulator-based reinforcement learning for data center cooling optimization
notes: Meta's penthouse outside-air/evaporative design, its three supply-air control loops, and offline RL trained in a physics-based simulator to set the airflow setpoint (about 20% less supply-fan energy, 4% less water). Template for the course's RL module.

title: DeepMind AI Reduces Google Data Centre Cooling Bill by 40%
notes: The original public result: an ML recommendation system cut cooling energy by about 40%. Motivating story for Modules 23-24.

title: Safety-first AI for autonomous data centre cooling and industrial control
notes: Autonomous cooling control: 5-minute snapshots from thousands of sensors, neural-network energy prediction, uncertainty filtering, two-layer verification against operator limits, operator override; savings grew from 12% to about 30% in kW/ton. Use as the safety-architecture reference in Module 27.

title: Data center cooling using model-predictive control
venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 31 (NeurIPS 2018)
notes: Floor-level MPC at Google: AHU fan speed and valve as controls; cold-aisle temperature and differential pressure as states; server power and entering water temperature as disturbances; linear model from about 3 h of safe exploration beat per-AHU PID loops. Directly shapes the simulator's air-side states and the MPC baseline.

title: Enabling 1 MW IT racks and liquid cooling at OCP EMEA Summit
notes: 48 V DC racks (10 to 100 kW), +/-400 V DC sidecar power for up to 1 MW racks, more than 500 kW per rack expected before 2030, liquid cooling across 2,000+ TPU pods at about 99.999% availability, redundant in-row CDUs (Project Deschutes).

title: Hardware - NVIDIA DGX GB Rack Scale Systems User Guide
notes: Vendor documentation for the GB200 NVL72 rack: about 120 kW, 18 liquid-cooled compute trays, eight 33 kW power shelves (6 x 5.5 kW PSUs, N+N) on a 50-51 V DC busbar, air-cooled networking and storage. Page is undated; year is approximate. Use for the AI-pod parameters.

title: OAI System Liquid Cooling Guidelines (OCP template, March 3, 2023 update)
authors: Open Compute Project, Open Accelerator Infrastructure sub-project
notes: Cold-plate loop design guidance for 1 kW-class accelerators: 1.25-2.0 L/min/kW (design 1.5 for a 10 K rise with PG25), case-to-inlet resistance below 0.02 K/W, coolant-supply temperature groups (40-45 C and 30-37 C). Primary source for the DLC loop parameters.

title: EnergyPlus 9.6 Engineering Reference: Zone Internal Gains (ElectricEquipment:ITE:AirCooled)
authors: U.S. Department of Energy, EnergyPlus development team
notes: Equations for air-cooled IT equipment: CPU and fan power vs load and inlet temperature, airflow vs load and inlet temperature, recirculation-adjusted inlet temperature, supply/return approach temperatures, supply heat index, power-supply losses vs part load. The simulator's IT model follows this structure.

title: EnergyPlus 9.6 Input Output Reference: Group Internal Gains (ITE objects)
authors: U.S. Department of Energy, EnergyPlus development team
notes: Input fields for the ITE object (design fan power fraction, airflow per watt, approach temperatures, power-supply efficiency curve, ASHRAE class used to count hours outside the allowable envelope).

title: EnergyPlus 9.6 Engineering Reference: Chillers (Electric EIR model)
authors: U.S. Department of Energy, EnergyPlus development team
notes: DOE-2-style chiller model with three curves (capacity and EIR vs leaving chilled-water and entering condenser temperature, EIR vs part-load ratio). Level 2a chiller option in the simulator.

title: EnergyPlus 9.6 Engineering Reference: Cooling Towers and Evaporative Fluid Coolers
authors: U.S. Department of Energy, EnergyPlus development team
notes: Merkel/effectiveness-NTU tower models, CoolTools and YorkCalc approach correlations for variable-speed towers, free convection, and makeup water as evaporation plus drift plus blowdown.

title: Making Large UPS Systems More Efficient (White Paper 108, Revision 3)
venue: Schneider Electric Data Center Science Center
notes: UPS efficiency curves and the no-load / proportional / square-law loss decomposition; eco-mode 98-99% vs 94-97% double conversion. Basis of the simulator's UPS loss polynomial. Year is approximate (revision cites sources accessed January 2012).

title: Data Center Temperature Rise During a Cooling System Outage (White Paper 179, Revision 0)
venue: Schneider Electric Data Center Science Center
notes: Well-mixed room model and CFD for power-outage transients: up to about 5 K/min heating, generator start, 10-15 min chiller restart, thermal storage sizing by rack density, effect of containment. Gives a quantitative validation scenario for the simulator. The link is a third-party host that serves the PDF as a direct download; year approximate.

title: Comparing UPS System Design Configurations (White Paper 75, Revision 4)
venue: Schneider Electric Data Center Science Center
notes: Compares capacity (N), isolated redundant, parallel redundant (N+1), distributed redundant and system-plus-system (2N, 2N+1) UPS designs. Metadata from a search listing; not opened.

title: Real-Time Data Center Transient Analysis
venue: ASME 2011 Pacific Rim Technical Conference and Exhibition on Packaging and Integration of Electronic and Photonic Systems (InterPACK2011)
notes: Peer-reviewed source of the well-mixed transient room model used in Schneider WP 179. Metadata confirmed via Crossref; full text needs library access.

title: Centrifugal chillers: Thermodynamic modelling and a diagnostic case study
notes: Gordon-Ng thermodynamic chiller model applied to diagnosing a real centrifugal chiller; parameters map to internal losses, heat leaks and heat-exchanger resistance. Level 2b chiller model and a natural FDD exercise. Crossref-verified; author initials from memory.

title: Predictive and diagnostic aspects of a universal thermodynamic model for chillers
venue: International Journal of Heat and Mass Transfer
notes: Companion paper presenting the general Gordon-Ng model and its predictive/diagnostic use. Crossref-verified.

title: Dimensionless Parameters for Evaluation of Thermal Design and Performance of Large-scale Data Centers
venue: 8th AIAA/ASME Joint Thermophysics and Heat Transfer Conference
notes: Origin of the Supply Heat Index and Return Heat Index for quantifying recirculation. Crossref-verified.

title: Rack Cooling Effectiveness in Data Centers and Telecom Central Offices: The Rack Cooling Index (RCI)
notes: Defines RCI_HI and RCI_LO; FEMP's guide recommends RCI for monitoring inlet temperatures. Citation from memory; URL is the generic ASHRAE Transactions page.

title: Dynamo: Facebook's Data Center-Wide Power Management System
venue: 2016 ACM/IEEE 43rd Annual International Symposium on Computer Architecture (ISCA)
notes: Fleet-wide power monitoring and capping that enables oversubscription; reference for the supervisory power-capping loop. Crossref-verified (first four authors listed).

title: Flex: High-Availability Datacenters With Zero Reserved Power
venue: 2021 ACM/IEEE 48th Annual International Symposium on Computer Architecture (ISCA)
notes: Microsoft design that uses the redundant power budget for workloads and sheds or caps flexible load during failures. Crossref-verified (first four authors listed; first names from memory).

title: Mitigating Curtailment and Carbon Emissions through Load Migration between Data Centers
notes: Quantifies how moving flexible compute between sites can absorb curtailed renewables and cut emissions; supports carbon-aware scheduling exercises. Crossref-verified.

title: Carbon-Aware Computing for Datacenters
notes: Google's system for shifting flexible compute to lower-carbon hours. Not opened by this agent; DOI taken from the sibling record in sources-domain-ml.json (which is verified there). First author only.

title: Rethinking Load Growth: Assessing the Potential for Integration of Large Flexible Loads in US Power Systems
venue: Nicholas Institute for Energy, Environment & Sustainability, Duke University
notes: Estimates 76/98/126 GW of new flexible load could be integrated with 0.25/0.5/1% annual curtailment. Figures and authors from memory; exact URL not checked.

title: Powering Intelligence: Analyzing Artificial Intelligence and Data Center Energy Consumption
notes: 2024 scenarios: data centers at 4.6-9.1% of US generation by 2030. Figures from news coverage of the report; exact product URL not checked.

title: Powering Intelligence 2026: Updated Scenarios of U.S. Data Center Electricity Use and Power Strategies
notes: 2026 update: 9-17% of US electricity by 2030 and much higher state shares (e.g., Virginia). Product URL from search results; figures from secondary coverage; not opened.

title: A labeled dataset for building HVAC systems operating in faulted and fault-free states
notes: LBNL labeled fault/fault-free HVAC data (simulated and experimental) to benchmark FDD methods alongside the simulator's injected faults. Crossref-verified; the ML sibling file holds the related 2020 dataset records.

title: Historical Climate Data
license: Open Government Licence - Canada (not checked on the page)
notes: Station-level hourly observations (temperature, dew point, RH, pressure, wind) with bulk CSV download; use for a BC Interior site (e.g., Kamloops) and for the 2021 heat-dome incident.

title: Global Hourly - Integrated Surface Database (ISD)
authors: NOAA National Centers for Environmental Information
license: US Government data, generally public domain for US-origin records (not checked; some non-US data carry WMO Resolution 40 restrictions)
notes: Global hourly surface observations from 100+ sources (temperature, dew point, pressure, wind, etc.); use for Columbia Plateau stations such as Moses Lake, Wenatchee, The Dalles or Yakima.

title: National Solar Radiation Database (NSRDB)
authors: National Renewable Energy Laboratory (now National Laboratory of the Rockies)
notes: Gridded satellite-derived solar and meteorological time series and TMY products for the Americas; license and 2026 update confirmed on data.gov. The nsrdb.nrel.gov domain did not resolve on the access date (lab renamed); look for the current host before use.

title: Repository of free climate data for building performance simulation (TMYx EPW files)
notes: Typical-year EnergyPlus weather files derived from ISD hourly data through 2023 (2026 release, 17,315 locations, ERA5 solar). Page content confirmed; author names from memory, so marked unverified. Best quick input for annual simulator runs.

title: Thermal Guidelines for Data Processing Environments, 5th edition
notes: The authoritative envelope definitions (A1-A4, H1, humidity, rate-of-change, liquid W classes) and server power/airflow vs inlet temperature data. ISBN 9781947192645 (catalog also lists 9781947192652); ISBNs from a library-catalog search result, not checked. Fetch via library.

title: Emergence and Expansion of Liquid Cooling in Mainstream Data Centers
notes: Free TC 9.9 white paper arguing that new facilities should be ready for liquid cooling. URL from search results; not opened.

title: Liquid Cooling Guidelines for Datacom Equipment Centers
notes: Design reference for facility-water and technology-cooling loops; FEMP (2024) says a third edition is upcoming. Edition year from memory; ISBN not captured.
